h: Guarding the Mouth Opens the Light of the Oral Torah

p: Why did she merit this place?
whoever guards his mouth and his tongue
merits to be clothed in ruach hakodesh.
This implies that even if one has already merited
to stand in spirit without body
(as mentioned above in the previous maamar),
רַק עַל יְדֵי דְּנָטַר פּוּמָא וְלִשָּׁנֵיהּ
except by guarding one's mouth and tongue.
"Who is the man who desires life,
who loves days to see good"
is "the light, that it was good,"
וְאֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא תוֹרָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה, א)
which means guarding only from evil;
לֹא הָיָה דְּבַר אִיסּוּר רַק רְשׁוּת
it was not a forbidden matter but an optional one.
רַק אֶפְשָׁר כֵּיוָן שֶׁמָּרְדְּכַי צִיוָּה עָלֶיהָ
One could say that since Mordechai commanded her
and he was of the Sanhedrin,
But the language of the holy Zohar,
"she guarded her mouth, not to tell anything,"
is not specifically about forbidden speech.
But it is brought in the Gemara (Shabbos 113b)
"from pursuing your affairs and speaking a word":
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה דִּיבּוּרְךָ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי
that your speech on Shabbos should not be, etc.;
who used to talk a great deal;
he said to her, "Mother, it is Shabbos,"
It appears that one should not speak
וְהִנֵּה אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רא, ב)
Now it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 201b)
and because Shabbos is called speech,
weekday speech is forbidden on Shabbos."
"the day of Shabbos in the year,
and the mouth in the soul."
And we have already said that the meaning is not
that the mouth was created on Shabbos,
spoke on Erev Shabbos as well;
Rather, the "mouth of Hashem" was created on Shabbos,
for a person to speak words of Torah,
And this is the meaning of "and speaking a word,"
and it is not written "and from speaking a word,"
for it should have said "and from speaking a word,"
that one not speak a forbidden word,
according to Rashi's explanation mentioned above.
Rather the meaning is that he should speak a word,
only that it be the word of Hashem;
and that is "the mouth of Hashem."
And this is what is said
בְּשֵׁם הָרַבִּי רַבִּי בֶּער זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
in the name of the Rebbe, Reb Ber, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
that it is possible even with words of Torah and prayer
"a person should always engage in Torah and mitzvos
even not for their own sake,"
as they said in the Gemara (Pesachim 50b),
and all the more so when he engages without specific intent
אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְעִנְיַן רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
But nevertheless, with regard to ruach hakodesh
so long as he does not speak
in the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem,"
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (עֵירוּבִין נד, ב)
And this is as we find in the Gemara (Eruvin 54b):
"'Speak' — these are the masters of Talmud,
all of whose conversation is words of Torah."
And this is "and speaking a word":
be words of Torah and "the mouth of Hashem."
we do not find at all
that he told his mother that it is forbidden to speak on Shabbos;
רַק הֲוָה אֲמַר לָהּ שַׁבְּתָא הוּא
only he would say to her, "It is Shabbos,"
Rather, Rashbi, all of whose conversation was Torah
the holiness of Shabbos shone upon her,
that one must speak only a word
that is the words of Hashem, the mouth of Hashem;
and she, who was not a woman of Torah,
And on Shabbos every one of Yisrael can
for Shabbos corresponds to the middah of Malchus,
we call it the Oral Torah";
and it is a spirit from the Holiness on High,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב, א)
and as the Ramban writes (on Bava Basra 12a):
"A sage is superior to a prophet"
and they are words of the living God,

p: like the question of Sefer HaBahir
Since it says "Let there be light,"
why is it written "and there was light"?
For "and it was so" would have sufficed!
for from the right the left goes forth, etc.
From here: the first "vayehi" in the Torah
was on the side of the left, etc.
which darkened the face of the world;
when the secret of Esav and his deeds was revealed,
"And Esav was a man who knew trapping"
to entice the people of the world, etc.
with what is written in Sefer HaBahir
And it is as is written above there
"and the Torah" is the Written Torah,
וְכֵן נִדְרָשׁ גַּם בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת ה, א)
And so it is expounded also in the Gemara (Berachos 5a):
(and so too writes Sefer HaBahir there).
And the holy Zohar says further there:
in two hundred and seven worlds, etc.";
and it says, in the count of 310 worlds:
That is, in the Oral Torah,
where there are forty-nine ways to declare pure
and forty-nine ways to declare impure;
and from them it branches off
that there are also paths from the yetzer hara,
which can make darkness into light,
"He appeared to him like a talmid chacham"
who makes himself out to be a teacher
who shows him a good path,
And this is what it says about "and there was light,"
that it is not a sign of blessing, etc.,
for from it went forth that darkness, etc.,
as it is written, "And Esav was one who knew trapping"
to entice the people of the world
so that they not walk on an upright path.
and he would show interpretations not according to the halachah:
that the matter of his golden calves
was, Heaven forbid, a service to Hashem
and that is making darkness into light.
אַךְ מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
But one who merits the Oral Torah
merits to reveal the light from within the darkness,
and to merit the dew of Atika
that is, the 207 from the right,
in which is truly included the first light.
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah, etc.,"
and they would have found everything in the Written Torah;
And this is the matter that it explained
"Let there be light" as the Written Torah
וַיְהִי אוֹר עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and "and there was light" as the Oral Torah:
that is, that the first light was hidden away,
and was hidden for those who toil in the Oral Torah
for they will bring out the light from within the darkness,
וְהוּא כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר
And it is like what is written in Sefer HaBahir
about the middah of Malchus (see above).
And so what it says there,
and put it for them in its place":
for Shabbos is the seventh middah, Malchus;
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah";
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
And this is "The stone the builders rejected":
Avraham and Yitzchak, who built the world,
were the essence of the Written Torah,
with which the two thousand years of Torah began,
after the two thousand years of chaos;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
This is not so of David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah,
וְהָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
and was the master of those who possess ruach hakodesh;
לָכֵן הוּא נַעֲשָׂה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת
therefore he became the chariot for the middah of Malchus,
the aspect of the Oral Torah,
to repair the "much anger" with "much wisdom."
וְרַק עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And only through the Oral Torah
זוֹכִין לְהוֹצִיא אוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הַחוֹשֶׁךְ דַּוְקָא
does one merit to bring light specifically out of the darkness,
to merit the first light that was hidden;
except that which comes out of the darkness"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ תְּצַוֶּה קפד, א)
(as it says in the holy Zohar, Tetzaveh 184a).
And this is "The stone the builders rejected
And on Shabbos every one of Yisrael
words of the living God, the mouth of Hashem,

and they can merit ruach hakodesh,
